A.explanation: Arrows point from $+1300\text{ V}$ to $+800\text{ V}$ which is correct for direction, but the edge lines curve inwards instead of bulging outwards.

B.explanation: Arrows point from $+1300\text{ V}$ to $+800\text{ V}$ and the central lines are parallel with edge lines bulging outwards, which is the correct uniform plus fringe field.

C.explanation: Arrows point from $+800\text{ V}$ to $+1300\text{ V}$, which is from low to high potential and opposite to the direction of the electric field.

D.explanation: Arrows point from $+800\text{ V}$ to $+1300\text{ V}$, so the field direction is reversed even though the outward fringe shape is shown.

hints: Notice the left plate is at $+800\text{ V}$ and the right plate is at $+1300\text{ V}$ - which plate is at higher potential?
Recall electric field lines point from high potential to low potential and must leave and meet the metal plates at right angles.
Compare the straight parallel lines in the middle with the curved fringe lines at the top and bottom - the correct fringe bulges outwards beyond the plates.
walkthrough: Identify the given potentials: left plate $+800\text{ V}$ and right plate $+1300\text{ V}$, so the potential decreases from right to left by $500\text{ V}$.
State the governing rule: electric field direction is from high potential to low potential, so here it must point from the $+1300\text{ V}$ plate toward the $+800\text{ V}$ plate, i.e. to the left.
This immediately rules out diagrams with arrows pointing to the right, leaving only the two diagrams with leftward arrows.
State the shape rule: between parallel plates the field is uniform in the centre, so lines are straight, parallel and equally spaced and perpendicular to the plates.
At the ends of the plates the field fringes, so the outer lines bulge outwards beyond the gap rather than curving inwards.
Only the diagram with leftward arrows, straight central lines and outward-bulging top and bottom lines satisfies both direction and shape. This is option B
